newsitem.title: USA: Canadian spot natgas strengthens in West on outage.
newsitem.headline: Canadian spot natgas strengthens in West on outage.

text.p: Canadian spot natural gas prices were slightly higher in the West Tuesday as an outage in British Columbia continued to keep supply fairly tight, traders said.

Westcoast Energy's Fort Nelson gas plant in northeastern B.C., with a maximum capacity of about 750 million cubic feet per day (mmcfd), is scheduled to be out of service until June 18 for maintenance.
As a result, prices at Sumas, Wash., rose another two cents to the low-$1.30s per million British thermal units (mmBtu).

According to Weather Services Corp, temperature highs throughout Washington were forecast to drop into the high-60s to low-70s F Wednesday and Thursday, creating little weather-related demand in the Northwest.
At the AECO storage hub in Alberta, prices were quoted about two cents higher at C$1.52-1.54 per gigajoule.
July AECO was also talked a little firmer at C$1.49-1.50 per GJ, while one-year was quoted at C$1.71.
"NOVA is starting to draft. Some field receipts still haven't shown up," one Calgary-based trader said, noting the absence of supplies from B.C. was supporting the market.
He also noted that daily storage injections in Alberta were about 750-800 million cubic feet.
In the East, prices at Niagara slipped three cents to the low-to-mid $2.30s per mmBtu in response to the softening on NYMEX.
July Henry Hub natgas futures fell to a low of $2.115, down 2.5 cents.
In Toronto, temperatures were forecast to reach a high of 82 degrees F on Wednesday but only 73 degrees F on Thursday, WSC said.
